🛍️ Retail Sales Analysis & Forecasting¶

👤 Author: Sarah Ahmed¶

📌 Objective:¶

This project analyzes historical retail sales data from a fictional superstore to uncover key business insights and forecast future sales. The analysis focuses on identifying sales trends, top-performing products, customer segments, and regions. A time series forecasting model (Prophet) is used to predict future sales, helping stakeholders make data-driven decisions for inventory planning and marketing strategies.

Dataset Source: Superstore Sales Dataset

🧰 Libraries Used¶

The following libraries are used throughout the project for data analysis, visualization, and forecasting:

  • pandas: To load, clean, and manipulate the dataset
  • matplotlib.pyplot: To create visualizations like bar charts and line plots
  • IPython.display: To display KPI summaries in a clean Markdown format
  • prophet: To build a time series model and forecast future sales
  • 💡 Note: Run !pip install prophet if you're using Prophet for the first time.
In [ ]:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

🧹 Convert Date Columns & Sort¶

To prepare the dataset for time series analysis and ensure chronological accuracy,
we convert the Order Date and Ship Date columns to datetime format using pd.to_datetime() with dayfirst=True (since the date format is DD/MM/YYYY).

We also sort the dataset by Order Date to maintain proper time sequence before any trend or forecasting analysis.

The first few rows of the cleaned data are displayed below, along with a summary of the dataset.

📈 Monthly Sales Trend¶

To analyze overall sales performance over time, we group the data by month using the Order Date column.
We convert it to a Period (Year-Month) format, aggregate total sales for each period, and plot the results.

This trend visualization helps identify:

  • High-performing months
  • Seasonal patterns
  • Overall business growth

The chart below shows the monthly sales trend throughout the dataset's timeline.

In [80]:
# Load your data (use the correct path)
df = pd.read_csv("/Users/mohamedhelill/Downloads/train.csv")

df["Order Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Order Date"], dayfirst=True)
df["Ship Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Ship Date"], dayfirst=True)

df.columns = df.columns.str.strip()

# Confirm column exists
print("✅ 'Sales' in columns:", "Sales" in df.columns)

# Fix date format
df["Order Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Order Date"], dayfirst=True)

# Group by Year-Month
monthly_sales = df.groupby(df["Order Date"].dt.to_period("M"))["Sales"].sum()

# Convert index to datetime
monthly_sales.index = monthly_sales.index.to_timestamp()

# Plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(monthly_sales.index, monthly_sales.values, marker='o')
plt.title("Monthly Sales Trend", fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Sales ($)")
plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

✅ 'Sales' in columns: True

🔮 Sales Forecasting with Facebook Prophet¶

To forecast future sales, we use Facebook Prophet, a powerful time series forecasting library designed for business applications.
We aggregate daily sales and train the model on historical data. Prophet automatically detects trends and seasonality, making it ideal for retail sales data.

In this section:

  • Sales are grouped by day and formatted for Prophet (ds, y)
  • A model is trained on historical sales data
  • Future dates (90 days ahead) are generated
  • A forecast is produced and visualized

The resulting forecast provides valuable insight into expected sales trends for the upcoming quarter.

In [87]:
# Aggregate daily sales
sales_daily = df.groupby("Order Date")["Sales"].sum().reset_index()

# Rename columns for Prophet
sales_daily.columns = ["ds", "y"]

# Initialize and fit the model
model = Prophet()
model.fit(sales_daily)

# Create future dataframe
future = model.make_future_dataframe(periods=90)

# Predict future sales
forecast = model.predict(future)


# Plot forecast
fig = model.plot(forecast)
plt.title("📈 Sales Forecast for Next 3 Months")
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Sales ($)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

📊 Forecast Components: Trend & Seasonality¶

Prophet not only predicts future values, but also breaks the forecast into meaningful components:

  • Trend: Long-term direction of sales over time
  • Weekly Seasonality: Day-of-week sales patterns (e.g., higher on Mondays)
  • Yearly Seasonality (if detected): Seasonal patterns throughout the year

These components help uncover hidden patterns that inform better inventory planning, marketing campaigns, and staffing strategies.

In [88]:
# Plot trend & seasonality components
model.plot_components(forecast)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

📤 Export Forecast Results to Excel¶

To share the forecast results with stakeholders or for further analysis in Excel or Power BI,
we select the relevant forecast columns and export them to an .xlsx file.

The exported file includes:

  • ds: Date
  • yhat: Predicted sales
  • yhat_lower and yhat_upper: Confidence interval bounds

This allows easy integration of forecasts into business reports, dashboards, or presentations.

In [44]:
# Select useful forecast columns
forecast_result = forecast[["ds", "yhat", "yhat_lower", "yhat_upper"]]

# Export to Excel
forecast_result.to_excel("sales_forecast.xlsx", index=False)

print("✅ Forecast exported to 'sales_forecast.xlsx'")

✅ Forecast exported to 'sales_forecast.xlsx'

📊 Retail Sales Analysis and Forecasting Report¶

✅ Final Conclusion¶

The Retail Sales Analysis and Forecasting project provided a comprehensive overview of sales performance over time. Through Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), trend evaluation, and time series forecasting using Prophet, the project successfully identified key sales patterns and projected future trends.

The analysis uncovered notable seasonality and demand fluctuations influenced by time of year and possibly promotional events. These findings are instrumental in guiding strategic planning, inventory management, and marketing activities. The forecasted sales for the next three months provide valuable insight for short-term decision-making and resource allocation.

💡 Business Insights¶

  1. Seasonality as a Sales Driver
    Sales volumes show recurring peaks and troughs, indicating strong seasonal behavior. This suggests the importance of aligning marketing and inventory plans with historical high-demand periods.

  2. Growth Potential with Optimization
    Despite fluctuations, the overall trend points to long-term growth. Consistent product availability, customer satisfaction initiatives, and data-backed decision-making can further boost sales.

  3. Forecasting Improves Planning Efficiency
    The ability to predict future sales enables proactive inventory, staffing, and budgeting decisions, reducing the risk of overstock or stockouts.

  4. Data Quality Gaps Identified
    The presence of missing or inconsistent values during the data cleaning phase indicates a need for improved data governance to ensure analysis reliability.

🛠️ Strategic Recommendations¶

  1. Establish a Data Management Process

    • Ensure real-time or daily updates to the sales database.
    • Assign a dedicated database manager to monitor data integrity and completeness.

  2. Leverage Seasonality for Marketing

    • Launch campaigns aligned with peak demand months.
    • Introduce discounts, bundles, or loyalty rewards during off-peak periods to maintain steady sales.

  3. Enhance Forecasting Accuracy

    • Integrate external factors such as holidays, weather, and economic trends to build more resilient models.
    • Continuously monitor model performance and update it with recent data.

  4. Adopt Business Intelligence Tools

    • Use visualization tools like Power BI or Tableau for real-time sales monitoring.
    • Automate reporting workflows to support timely, data-driven decisions across departments.

  5. Segment Customers for Deeper Insights

    • Analyze sales by customer segments to identify high-value clients and tailor offerings to their preferences.
    • Use segmentation insights for targeted campaigns and personalized promotions.

  6. Optimize Inventory Based on Forecasts

    • Align procurement cycles with projected demand to minimize holding costs and lost sales.
    • Monitor fast-moving vs. slow-moving products and adjust stocking strategies accordingly.
